Fresh off their June 2026 debut album release, Star Time returns to the Wellington Jazz Festival for yet another epic showdown at San Fran!

Star Time is a high energy Afrobeat jazz ensemble which arose from the ever growing jazz and African music scenes in Te-Whanganui-A-Tara. Led by the charismatic Rwandan-born vocalist Francois Judah, and backed by a massive 8-piece band, they aim to deliver a sonically unforgettable experience in the form of traditional Afrobeat dance rhythms, and spontaneous live arrangements which have set audiences on fire since their formation in 2024.

Star Time has continuously honed in on their signature fusion of afrobeat, dance music and jazz in a way that highlights their undeniably contagious energy as a group. Releasing their debut album ‘WE ARE HERE’ in 2026, this body of work boldly cemented their sound, rooted in homage to African music and rhythms, with the aim of uniting all people on the dance floor.

Join us at Zealandia these school holidays for a free, nature inspired craft event delivered by local artists!

Tayla Hartemink has designed a series of unique stamps featuring beautiful native manu, rākau, mokomoko, and ika, perfect for decorating cards, and printing fabric and clothing. The designs feature kupu Māori/Māori words, and are a fun, simple way for whānau to practice te reo Māori.

A limited amount of materials will be provided, but we encourage you to bring your own T-shirts, tote bags, tea towels, or other fabric items to personalise with these stunning designs.

Tayla Hartemink (Tūhoe) is a multi-media artist, illustrator and creative workshop facilitator based in Te-Whanganui-ā-Tara. Tayla’s work is rooted in a deep connection to whakapapa and indigenous storytelling. Her work incorporates graphic design, painting, print-making and traditional motifs. Through her artwork she hopes to inspire and empower people to connect with te ao Māori.

Suitable for all ages— drop in, get hands-on, and make something colourful to take home!

Koha / gold coin donation appreciated to help cover costs.

This event will be held on the 7th and 10th of October, 10am-3pm in the Zealandia Visitor Centre Foyer. Standard entry fees apply if entering the sanctuary. Members get free entry!

AI and Your Kids: An Open Conversation with Marianne Malmstrom | Te Matapihi Central Library
Children typically explore and adopt new technological tools before their parents do. Artificial intelligence (AI) is no exception. So where does that leave parents?

Join veteran educator Marianne Malmstrom, co-author of Literacies for AI-Ready Humans, for an open conversation about raising children in an AI-shaped world. No technical knowledge is required, and your questions set the agenda.

This isn't a conversation about whether AI is good or bad, nor a session of fear, hype, or one-size-fits-all answers. Instead, the conversation will explore the questions that matter most: What do children need from us? How do they develop the filter between their ears, the one no app can install? And why might the relationship you already have with your child become the most protective thing in your toolkit?

Marianne Malmstrom is an internationally recognised educator and researcher with 45 years of experience, the last 25 specialising in the intersection of learning and emerging technologies. Her work supports students, teachers, schools and families as they navigate the opportunities and challenges new technologies bring. Learn more about her work on her blog, Follow the Learning.

Register for this discussion using the ticketing link.

If you can't make this session, Marianne is leading two other discussions. Find them on our event calendar: https://wellingtoncitylibraries.trumba.com/?search=marianne

long_description:
OvO (Italy) at Valhalla, Wellington with Wince and Dreamweb
Catch genre defying Italian noise duo - OvO, Sunday, October 25th (Labour day weekend!) 2026 at Valhalla .

Deftly navigating between noise rock, doom, extreme and blackened metal, industrial sludge and even electronica. “Decibel Magazine” have perhaps described them best by hailing the bands sound as “a David Lynch dance party”. Italy’s ovoband , continue to rewrite the definition of what alternative music can be. Something which New Zealand audiences can look forward to seeing this October 2026.

Formed by Stefania Pedretti and Bruno Dorella in Milan, Italy in the late 90s. OvO have taken their inspiration from the likes of Suicide, Swans, and Diamana Galas. Centred around the ear piercing banshee-like vocals of Stefania, and a constant guitar drone and dark menace as the undercurrent of their songs. AELERT Regulatory Masterclass on Regulatory Integrity, Ethics and Professionalism ft. Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole

October 30 | Te Iho (Bowen House)

Integrity is the foundation of regulatory legitimacy. When it holds, regulators make defensible decisions, resist undue influence and retain public trust. When it slips, the damage is slow, quiet and hard to reverse.

This masterclass brings together two of Aotearoa's most respected regulatory leaders, Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole, in central Wellington to work through what integrity, ethics and professionalism require in practice, and how agencies can strengthen them deliberately rather than assume they will hold.

long_description:
La Dispute - No One Was Driving The Car Aotearoa tour - Wellington
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.

﻿

It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.

﻿

Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

About the speakers

John Grace

John Grace is a commercial lawyer and amateur photographer. John’s black and white photos of Futuna Chapel have been taken on an old tripod camera using 1866 French lenses. A selection of his photos will be exhibited at the Chapel.

Catherine Hammond

"Against Forgetting: Photographic Archives in Aotearoa"

Catherine Hammond is the director of collections and research at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum. She was formerly Hocken Librarian at the University of Otago Te Whare Wānanga o Ōtākou, and before that head of documentary heritage at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum and research library manager at Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki. She co-edited of ‘A Different Light/First Photography of Aotearoa’ (2024).

The Jackson Street Quest!
This Festival event runs from the 24 October to the 15 November 2026.


Have fun and learn at the same time! Go on a quest to discover historic Jackson Street, and bring the family / whanau along with you.

Go on a Quest (scavenger hunt) along Jackson Street, exploring our history, searching for clues about the area’s shops, industries, sport, and the people who helped build the community.

As each clue is solved, you discover how Jackson Street grew to become the heart of the lively historic neighbourhood it is today.

• OR pick up a sheet from Bin Inn Petone, 211 Jackson Street (open 7 days per week)

• Start from the Historic Police Station, 274B Jackson Street
• Bring a pen
• The Quest can be done anytime of the day
• Takes approx. 45 minutes

For those 4-9yrs & 10yrs + :
When you have completed the Quest, return your sheet (with your contact details) to the black entry box by the front door of the Historic Police Station to go into a draw to win prizes!

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/the-jackson-street-quest/

Children need to be supervised by an adult at all times due to the busy nature of Jackson Street's road.
